duoNoel.modesDesc: The 12 questions are the same in both cases. Together, you each answer separately and the quiz looks for the Christmas duo that's most like your couple.
duoNoel.modeDuoMeta: Your Christmas duo and where you disagree
duoNoel.setupDescDuo: Enter your first names. The first person answers the 12 questions and then passes the phone. At the end, you'll see the Christmas duo you make and the questions where you don't agree.
duoNoel.setupDescSolo: The quiz asks 12 questions about how you celebrate Christmas, for example about the tree or Christmas morning. Answer with your couple in mind and you'll see which Christmas duo you make.
duoNoel.chacunMeme: On your own, you would each have got the same duo. You do Christmas the same way!
duoNoel.chacunGagne: Your duo is {{nom}}'s duo. {{autre}} gave it a lot of points too.
duoNoel.chacunCompromis: Your duo isn't the one either of you got alone. It's the one with the most points when your answers are added up.
duoNoel.chacunContraste: {{nom}} answered like Scrooge and {{autre}} like someone who loves Christmas. That's exactly this duo!
duoNoel.accordHaut: You see Christmas in more or less the same way.
duoNoel.accordMoyen: You agree on the main things but there are two or three traditions left to talk about.
duoNoel.accordBas: You don't celebrate Christmas the same way at all. You'll have to take a bit of each one's traditions!
duoNoel.jaugesTitre: The duos that are most like you
duoNoel.invitationDuo: And how does your partner see Christmas? Take the quiz again together to see which questions you disagree on.
duoNoel.noteFin: This quiz is a game, just for fun. The photos were created for this page.
duoNoel.modeDuoDesc: You each answer the 12 questions on the same phone, without seeing the other's answers.
duoNoel.modeSolo: On my own, for our couple
duoNoel.modeSoloDesc: You answer with your couple in mind.
duoNoel.relaisDebut: Answer the 12 questions, then pass the phone.
duoNoel.relaisSuite: {{nom}} is done. Your turn, no peeking at their answers!
duoNoel.memesReponsesUne: Just one identical answer out of {{total}}.
duoNoel.p_noel_d: At your place, Christmas is planned well ahead. Your lists are written in November and your presents are wrapped before anyone else's. The family usually ends up at your house. What you like best is the look on people's faces when they open their presents.
duoNoel.p_noel_a: By looking after everyone else, you end up last. Keep one evening for a date night over the holidays.
duoNoel.p_lutins_d: You love making things for Christmas. You make your own presents and your parcels are always beautifully wrapped. You've stayed big kids and December is the month when you can finally show it!
duoNoel.p_lutins_a: Start earlier this year. When you make a present at midnight on the 23rd, you get glue everywhere and it often ends in a row.
duoNoel.p_epices_d: For you, Christmas is mostly about cooking. You've been thinking about the menu since the fall and you go to the market to find good ingredients. You can even make the dessert twice if the first one isn't pretty enough. The kitchen is where you spend the holidays and it's where you're happiest.
duoNoel.p_epices_a: You can cook together, but decide beforehand who's the chef. Also remember to keep a few cookies for yourselves.
duoNoel.p_tomtes_d: You spend Christmas in your living room with a blanket and candles. You have a cheese fondue in front of a movie you know by heart. You don't need to go out or to see lots of people. You're perfectly happy at home, like the little Scandinavian gnomes who watch over the house.
duoNoel.p_tomtes_a: You're allowed to say no to every other invitation without feeling guilty. Also treat yourselves to a really nice blanket, it will get a lot of use.
duoNoel.p_neige_d: You spend Christmas outdoors whenever you can. You like walks in the cold and real trees that smell of the forest. You don't need ten strings of lights or three Christmas dinners. A little snow is enough to make you happy.
duoNoel.p_neige_a: If it doesn't snow where you live this year, go to the mountains for a weekend. Remember to take a thermos!
duoNoel.p_noisette_t: The Nutcracker and the Sugar Plum Fairy
duoNoel.p_noisette_d: You love everything that sparkles at Christmas, like the shop windows and the Christmas markets. At your place, the table is beautiful and the tree is nicely decorated. You dress up for Christmas Eve even when it's just you.
duoNoel.p_noisette_a: Give each other an outing rather than an object, for example a ballet or an evening at the ice rink. That's the kind of memory you keep for a long time.
duoNoel.p_rennes_d: At Christmas, you spend a lot of time on the road. You have dinner with one family and lunch with the other, with a trunk full of presents. Everyone is waiting for you and you always make it, even two hours late.
duoNoel.p_rennes_a: All that driving is tiring. Keep one day with no car and no invitations over the holidays so you can rest.
duoNoel.p_scrooge_d: At your place, one of you rolls their eyes at the first Christmas song and the other has already got the decorations out. It may also be that each of you grumbles, but you still end up in front of the tree. It's like in Dickens's tale, where the grump ends up loving Christmas.
duoNoel.p_scrooge_a: Make a deal. The one who loves Christmas chooses one tradition and the other gets one evening without a single string of lights.
duoNoel.q1: The Christmas decorations come out of their boxes:
duoNoel.q1c: Whenever we find a free weekend
duoNoel.q2a: Tall and decorated like a shop window
duoNoel.q2b: Covered in handmade ornaments and keepsakes
duoNoel.q2c: A real one that smells of the forest
duoNoel.q2d: Small or no tree at all, we're never home
duoNoel.q3a: A list for each person, all bought by early December
duoNoel.q3c: One nice present that we buy together
duoNoel.q3d: At the last minute, if at all
duoNoel.q4a: At our place, and we're the ones hosting
duoNoel.q4b: On the road, between two families
duoNoel.q5a: We cook for two days, and it's the best part
duoNoel.q5b: A beautiful table and we dress up
duoNoel.q5c: Everyone brings a dish, no fuss
duoNoel.q5d: Cheese fondue, a blanket and a movie
duoNoel.q6a: On repeat from November, we know all the words
duoNoel.q6c: In the car, to get through the miles
duoNoel.q6d: One sings, the other puts headphones on
duoNoel.q7a: The Christmas market for the mulled wine and the lights
duoNoel.q7b: A long walk in the cold
duoNoel.q7d: Couch, hot chocolate and a Christmas movie
duoNoel.q8a: We gave one to the whole family
duoNoel.q8b: One of us wears one, the other rolls their eyes
duoNoel.q8c: A big warm sweater, Christmas or not
duoNoel.q9b: Dinner with one side, lunch with the other
duoNoel.q9c: A small group suits us fine
duoNoel.q9d: We love them but two days is enough
duoNoel.q10a: Up first to see everyone's faces at the presents
duoNoel.q10b: A breakfast that lasts until noon
duoNoel.q10c: A lie-in and presents under the covers
duoNoel.q11: What you like best about Christmas:
duoNoel.q11b: The lights and the shop windows
duoNoel.q12a: We head off again to see people
duoNoel.q12b: We get out the puzzles and the board games
duoNoel.q12c: The mountains or the great outdoors if we can
duoNoel.q12d: We don't see anyone and it's lovely
